stories.title: New AIIMS hospitals record six crore consultations
stories.summary: The 18 fully functional new AIIMS hospitals have recorded over six crore outpatient consultations since 2021-22. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare says the milestone reflects the institutions' growing reach in providing specialised tertiary healthcare. Consultations have nearly tripled over the last five years.

stories.title: AIIMS population counter nears 1.5 billion
stories.summary: A digital billboard outside AIIMS in New Delhi has gone viral for displaying a population count of over 1.48 billion. The counter, which updates in real time, shows the nation is roughly 18.4 million people away from the 1.5 billion mark. The board remains a popular attraction.

stories.title: BIMSTEC health ministers agree on regional plan
stories.summary: Health ministers from seven BIMSTEC countries have adopted a five-year plan for regional health cooperation. The group also agreed that India will host a new Centre for Traditional Medicine in Jamnagar. This marks the first time the grouping has held a meeting dedicated entirely to health.

stories.title: India reports 38 percent drop in TB mortality
stories.summary: India has recorded a 38 percent reduction in tuberculosis mortality since 2015, surpassing the global average of 35 percent. According to the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026, the country also maintains a 94 percent treatment success rate for patients with drug-susceptible TB.

stories.title: Police investigate assault on flower seller near AIIMS
stories.summary: Delhi police have registered a case after a video showed a woman being beaten with sticks near the All India Institute of Medical Sciences. The incident reportedly occurred after the flower seller refused to sell drugs. Authorities are currently working to identify the attackers.

stories.title: Study links air pollution to rising blood sugar
stories.summary: A study of 12,064 adults found that higher exposure to fine particulate matter correlates with an increased likelihood of developing type 2 diabetes. Data from the National Family Health Survey shows that high blood sugar rates among Indian adults have risen since the previous survey.

stories.title: Delhi billboard tracks population growth
stories.summary: A digital billboard near AIIMS in South Delhi is displaying India’s population as exceeding 1.48 billion. The display gives the impression of a real-time count, though it is based on demographic projections and United Nations estimates rather than an official census. The board is currently counting projections.

stories.title: New AIIMS hospitals report rising patient numbers
stories.summary: New AIIMS hospitals established under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana have recorded over six crore outpatient consultations since 2021. The health ministry says the figures reflect the growing reach of the institutions, with annual consultations rising from 50 lakh in 2021 to 144 lakh this year.

stories.title: Telangana investigates illegal egg collection
stories.summary: The Telangana Health Department has inspected 27 Assisted Reproductive Technology facilities following reports of an illegal oocyte collection racket. Officials identified 13 regulatory violations across seven hospitals and issued show-cause notices. The state health minister has directed a comprehensive investigation into activities conducted under the guise of medical care.

stories.title: AIIMS director discusses diabetes trends
stories.summary: AIIMS director Dr. Nikhil Tandon has addressed common questions regarding the rising prevalence of type 2 diabetes in young adults. He explains that remission is not a cure and notes that gestational diabetes significantly increases future risk. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Health ministry proposes new registration framework
stories.summary: The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions has proposed a regulatory framework for the registration of healthcare workers. The plan outlines provisions for skill upgrades and proficiency assessments. The ministry aims to ensure greater uniformity and accountability in the registration of allied and healthcare professionals.

stories.title: Dengue fever cases decline in Sudan
stories.summary: Health officials in Sudan’s Sennar state report a decline in dengue fever cases. The ministry of health provided the update on the local situation, though further details on the scope of the outbreak were not immediately available.

stories.title: US faces potential loss of measles elimination status
stories.summary: The United States could lose its measles-free status this week as experts review a surge in cases. The country has confirmed 5,182 cases so far in 2026, the highest number since the early 1990s. Only 4 percent of these cases were among people known to be vaccinated.

stories.title: India and Bangladesh ban paraquat
stories.summary: India and Bangladesh have banned the pesticide paraquat to support suicide prevention and brain health. Globally, one in five suicides are attributed to the ingestion of toxic pesticides. Long-term exposure to such chemicals is also linked to neurological risks among agricultural workers and developmental disorders in children.

stories.summary: Gaza’s Health Ministry says an Israeli strike on a hospital killed 6 people CAIRO -- Gaza’s Health Ministry says an Israeli strike on a hospital killed 6 people. The full piece is for subscribers, and the headline is all that is public for now.

stories.title: Israeli strike hits Nasser Hospital in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Hospital complex in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon, according to the Hamas-run health ministry. The Israeli military stated it targeted a Hamas commander, though it provided no evidence. One of the two missiles fired did not explode.

stories.title: Six killed, 20 wounded in Israeli strike on hospital, Gaza Health Ministry says
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Hospital complex in Khan Yunis, southern Gaza, killed six people, including a surgeon, and wounded more than 20 others early Thursday, Gaza's Health Ministry and civil defense service said. stories.title: US measles status under review
stories.summary: A panel of experts is considering whether the United States has lost its measles elimination status. If revoked, the country would join several nations where the disease has returned after being eliminated. Dr. Paul Offit described the potential change as a tremendous step backwards for public health.

stories.title: Happiest Health to invest Rs 500 crore in digital health
stories.summary: Happiest Health will invest Rs 500 crore over five years to enter the digital healthcare market. The venture, promoted by Ashok Soota, plans to launch 11 applications within 18 months. The company aims to consolidate fragmented services onto an integrated platform. It is a crowded space to join.

stories.title: EkaCare partners with NHA for AI voice scribing
stories.summary: The National Health Authority has selected EkaCare to deploy an ambient AI voice scribe for public healthcare doctors. The tool uses the company's Parrotlet-A 2.5 Pro model to convert consultations into structured clinical notes. The goal is to reduce documentation workloads for staff under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission.

stories.title: Akara raises $5.5 million for hospital AI
stories.summary: Dublin-based health-tech startup Akara has raised $5.5 million in venture funding, bringing its total to $12.3 million. The Trinity College Dublin spin-out develops AI and sensor technology for hospital operations. The company plans to use the capital to accelerate adoption and expand its engineering teams in Ireland.

stories.title: Government plans AI-led upgrade for Ayushman Bharat
stories.summary: The central government intends to integrate AI into the Ayushman Bharat insurance scheme to automate claims processing and improve fraud detection. The initiative also includes digitising medical records to increase efficiency. The government says every rupee spent on healthcare must lead to better care for the people.

stories.title: NHA Chooses EkaCare for AI Voice Scribe Solution
stories.summary: The National Health Authority (NHA) has selected Bengaluru-based health AI startup EkaCare as a technology partner for its ambient AI-enabled Voice Scribe solution, which aims to reduce documentation for doctors in public health facilities. “With the Voice Scribe, a doctor can speak with the patient

stories.summary: The new All India Institute of Medical Sciences hospitals established under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana have recorded over six crore outpatient consultations since 2021. The health ministry stated this reflects the growing reach of the institutions in providing specialised tertiary care across the country.

stories.title: Deepinder Goyal launches Rs 85,000 wellness wearable
stories.summary: Deepinder Goyal has introduced Temple, a head-worn wellness wearable priced at Rs 85,000. Goyal stated the product is not made for India and expects less than 1 percent of sales to occur domestically. It is a rare pioneer product launch that flips the traditional low-cost model.

stories.title: AIIMS hosts global conference on mental health stigma
stories.summary: The 11th Together Against Stigma Conference began on 12 November at AIIMS New Delhi. Organised by The George Institute for Global Health and UNICEF India, the three-day event gathers experts to discuss reducing mental health stigma. The conference focuses on practical actions to improve access to care.

stories.title: Cross-National Study Evaluates Digital Mental Health Policies Across 40
stories.summary: A comparative analysis evaluating digital mental health policies across 40 countries has revealed substantial disparities in governance, strategic focus, and policy breadth between national income tiers. Investigating how governments guide the integration of digital health technologies into mental health services, researchers found that while international

stories.summary: Young people frequently turn to social media platforms to cope with mental health challenges, engaging in online self-disclosure of conditions such as anxiety and depression. stories.title: Digital mental health platform sees high satisfaction
stories.summary: A three-year study of the enhance platform across six German universities found high user satisfaction, though only 26 percent of participants attended an individual counselling session. Researchers noted that while students reported well-being gains, the uptake of one-on-one support remained modest. Satisfaction does not always imply engagement.

stories.title: Weekly park visits linked to better child mental health
stories.summary: Children who visit a park at least once a week may show better social-emotional development, according to a University of Exeter study of 4,219 youngsters. Researchers analysed data from the Children of the 90s Study to reach the conclusion. The findings suggest communities require accessible and safe green spaces.

stories.title: Study links irregular sleep to anxiety and depression
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of California analysed data from 20,000 wearable device users and found that irregular sleep schedules may worsen anxiety and depression. The study suggests that consistency in sleep-wake patterns is as significant as sleep duration. The body's clock prefers a predictable routine.

stories.title: Reddit mental health advice comes with a warning
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Medical Xpress reports that online mental health advice on platforms like Reddit carries inherent risks for users seeking guidance. The site currently limits access to the article, suggesting readers wait before attempting to view the content again.

stories.title: Mental health struggles can double veterans risk of heart disease
stories.summary: PTSD, depression, and anxiety can raise a veteran risk of major cardiovascular disease by 100 percent. While VA care often matches or exceeds other providers, only 32 percent of veterans who screen positive for depression pursue follow-up care. Help remains available, if not used.

stories.title: Treating nightmares early may lead more trauma survivors to access mental health care
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Medical Xpress reports on research regarding the treatment of nightmares as a gateway to broader mental health care for trauma survivors. The site currently limits access to the article, suggesting readers wait before attempting to view the content again.

stories.title: Study finds structured discrepancies between adolescent and parent mental health reports
stories.summary: Research indicates that agreement between adolescents and parents on mental health evaluations is often only moderate. Investigators used the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire to examine these reporting differences through variable and person centered techniques. Parents and children continue to see the same situation differently.

stories.title: Wearable sleep data linked to mental health symptoms
stories.summary: A study of 22,894 participants found that lower sleep regularity, measured by wearable devices, correlates with increased depression, anxiety, and loneliness. Researchers used the Sleep Regularity Index to compare symptoms across severity categories. The device has successfully tracked the correlation between rest and mood.

research.title: Common forever chemicals linked to nearly double the rate of aggressive breast cancer
research.summary: An NIH study found that women with high levels of two common “forever chemicals” had up to 93% higher rates of an aggressive form of breast cancer. The discovery raises concerns about the potential health effects of persistent chemicals found in everyday products.

research.title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 12 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04712-z In a prespecified companion study (BMT CTN 1801) of the randomized phase 3 BMT CTN 1703 trial comparing two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens, microbiome diversity at engraftment did not associate with non-relapse mortality, but secondary analyses found baseline microbiome diversity.

research.title: Scientists discover a common sugar may help cancer cells break free and spread
research.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising way that fructose, a sugar commonly found in sweetened foods and drinks, may help aggressive ovarian cancer spread. Researchers discovered that cancer cells surviving chemotherapy release fructose that weakens the bonds holding neighboring tumor cells together, making it easier for cancer to spread.

research.title: Stronger flu shot linked to nearly 55% lower Alzheimer's risk
research.summary: A surprising new study suggests that a stronger flu shot could offer older adults significantly greater protection against Alzheimer's disease. Researchers at UTHealth Houston analyzed nearly 200,000 adults ages 65 and older and found that those who received a high-dose influenza vaccine had a nearly 55% lower risk.
